title: Competitor features → customer journey mapping and ops-trigger matrix
creator: Evelyn Huang
description: Synthesize competitor feature sets into a customer-journey-aligned map and produce an operations-trigger matrix that recommends product, pricing, and routing responses for different competitive moves. Purpose is to turn model-landscape signals into actionable playbooks for Redwood sales, solutions engineering, and the runtime/ops teams.
objectives: Create a crosswalk that maps competitor features (e.g., low-latency inference tiers, quantization variants, private deployment controls) to specific buyer moments and functional needs.

Define an ops-trigger matrix that prescribes which internal levers (pricing, dedicated capacity recommendations, rollout fallbacks, region routing) to change when a competitor introduces or promotes a capability.
Deliver a concise exec brief and a prioritized list of experiments (pricing/packaging and product messaging) that sales can use in RFPs and renewals.
deliverables: Executive brief summarizing 3 strategic responses and recommended experiments
Lab plan for 2 pricing/packaging experiments and 1 routing policy pilot
acceptance_criteria: Crosswalk covers top 12 competitors and 8 buyer moments (onboarding, POC, scale, compliance, cost optimization, edge deployment, latency-sensitive, multi-region).
Ops-trigger matrix includes clear owner, signals to watch, recommended action, estimated impact, and rollback criteria for each trigger.
Exec brief reviewed and approved by GTM lead and Head of Product (sign-offs captured in comments).
research_plan: 1. Inventory competitor public docs, pricing pages, and recent product announcements (team: market-intel).
2. Interview 4 customer-facing reps (AE/SE/CS) for specific win/loss anecdotes tied to competitor features.
3. Run lightweight experiments in sandbox (routing/cost simulations) to estimate delta for recommended responses.
4. Validate with Solutions Eng on operational feasibility and with Legal for contractual implications.
initial_findings: Several competitors emphasize low-latency burst tiers that undercut hosted token pricing but with limited regional coverage — opportunity to highlight Dedicated for predictable SLA-sensitive customers.

A few suppliers bundle quantized model variants into lower-cost plans; customers care about predictable quality regressions — recommend explicit quantization profiles and quality SLAs in pricing experiments.
Private/VPC feature parity is becoming a disclosure point in RFPs; gaps exist in audit log surface area and KMS integrations that Redwood Private can emphasize.
next_steps: Complete crosswalk draft and circulate to GTM for feedback by 2026-03-12.
Bake two pricing experiments into the Growth backlog and create measurement dashboard IDs for impact tracking.
Prepare a one-page exec brief for the 2026-03-18 strategy sync.

risk_summary: Risk: Mis-characterizing competitor performance leading to wrong pricing moves. Mitigation: validate with SE and run small-scale pilots.
Risk: Legal/regulatory constraints for pilot pricing in some regions. Mitigation: route experiments through Legal before customer outreach.
Risk: Signal noise from rapid model announcements. Mitigation: define signal thresholds and re-check crosswalk weekly for 6 weeks post-delivery.
